gaps.sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
gaps.explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.

gaps.sentence: The parcels ___ (deliver) every morning before the shop opens.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for regular, repeated actions: are delivered.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

gaps.sentence: By next June, the entire collection ___ (move) to the new wing.
gaps.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle for something finished by 'next June'.

gaps.sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

gaps.sentence: The tickets ___ at the door from seven o'clock.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: can be + collected. The tickets are collected by the buyers.

gaps.sentence: The ancient scrolls are far too brittle ___ .
gaps.explanation: The scrolls receive the action: passive infinitive to be + unrolled.
